alerts.title: Rising creatinine and declining eGFR on TDF
alerts.message: TDF is associated with renal toxicity including declining eGFR. Creatinine has risen steadily from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m² and proteinuria 1+. This 5-year progressive decline while on TDF strongly suggests TDF-associated nephrotoxicity. DTG can also cause a small creatinine increase via inhibition of tubular secretion, but the magnitude and progressive trend here exceeds what DTG alone typically explains. Non-drug causes including chronic kidney disease from other etiologies should also be evaluated. The urinalysis showing proteinuria further supports renal injury. No clinician plan was documented for this abnormality.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate renal function trends and consider switching TDF to TAF or alternative. Investigate proteinuria and non-drug causes of CKD. Refer to nephrology if indicated.

alerts.title: No clinician plan documented despite abnormal labs
alerts.message: Guidelines require monitoring and management of adverse drug events and toxicities. The clinician's assessment and plan section is blank despite creatinine of 1.4 mg/dL, eGFR of 52, and proteinuria 1+. These abnormalities warrant active clinical decision-making: renal evaluation, potential regimen modification, and further investigation of proteinuria. The absence of any documented plan represents a guideline deviation and a patient safety gap.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and management plan addressing renal function decline and proteinuria. Consider regimen adjustment and nephrology referral.

alerts.title: Frequent ibuprofen use with renal impairment
alerts.message: Patient takes ibuprofen 400mg 2-3 times weekly for 6 months. NSAIDs can worsen renal function, particularly in patients with existing renal impairment. With eGFR at 52 and proteinuria already present, concurrent NSAID use compounds risk of further kidney injury. TDF nephrotoxicity plus NSAID-associated afferent arteriole vasoconstriction creates compounding renal risk. The mild fatigue reported may be unrelated but could reflect early renal or hematological issues.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to minimize or discontinue ibuprofen use. Consider alternative analgesics such as acetaminophen. Monitor renal function closely.

alerts.title: Monitoring gaps: renal and metabolic labs overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines list hyperglycemia/diabetes and abnormal weight gain as adverse events to monitor, particularly with DTG-containing regimens. Urinalysis shows trace glucose, which warrants fasting blood glucose testing. Additionally, proteinuria 1+ with declining eGFR requires urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and renal investigation. No orders for these follow-up tests were documented. Regular monitoring of renal function is essential given TDF use and confirmed renal impairment.

evidence.recommended_action: Order fasting blood glucose, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and repeat renal function panel. Monitor weight trends at each visit.
